simple: `AvatarEditorService` lets your game look at and change a player's real Roblox avatar. With the player's permission, you can see items they own, search the Marketplace, save a new look to their account, and save outfits. This lets you build a dressing room or outfit shop right inside your game.
analogy: It is like a clothing store with a fitting room. The store has to ask before looking in your closet, you can try on anything, but you only take home clothes you already own or buy.
keyPoints: Before reading a player's inventory, ask permission with `PromptAllowInventoryReadAccess()` once per session.
Check the answer with the `PromptAllowInventoryReadAccessCompleted` event. `Enum.AvatarPromptResult.Success` means yes.
`GetInventory()` returns the items the player owns, filtered by asset types like back or shoulder accessories.
`SearchCatalog()` searches the Marketplace using a `CatalogSearchParams` object with filters like price, keyword, and creator.
`PromptSaveAvatar()` saves a `HumanoidDescription` as the player's current avatar. `PromptCreateOutfit()` saves it as an outfit without replacing their avatar.
Players do not get items they do not own just by saving an outfit. Check with `MarketplaceService:PlayerOwnsAsset()` and offer `PromptPurchase()`.
If you do not want to sell items, you can let players favorite them with `PromptSetFavorite()` instead.

terms.inventory: All the avatar items a player owns on their Roblox account.
terms.Marketplace: Roblox's shop of avatar items, also called the catalog.
terms.prompt: A pop-up window that asks the player to agree to something, like letting the game see their items.
terms.HumanoidDescription: An object that lists everything about how a character looks: body parts, colors, clothes, and accessories.
terms.outfit: A saved look on a player's account that they can switch to later.
terms.asset type: The kind of item, like `BackAccessory` or `ShoulderAccessory`.
terms.pages object: Results that come in pages, like a book. `GetCurrentPage()` gives you the items on the page you are looking at.
terms.yield: Pause the script until something finishes. `PromptSaveAvatar()` does not yield, so you listen to an event to get the result.
terms.RigType: Whether the character body is R15 or R6.
terms.commission: Robux your game earns when a player buys an item inside it.

example.title: Save the player's current look as an outfit
example.code:
local AvatarEditorService = game:GetService("AvatarEditorService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local character = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

-- Read what the character is wearing right now
local description = humanoid:GetAppliedDescription()

-- Ask the player if they want to save it as an outfit
AvatarEditorService:PromptCreateOutfit(description, humanoid.RigType)

-- Wait for their answer
local result = AvatarEditorService.PromptCreateOutfitCompleted:Wait()
if result == Enum.AvatarPromptResult.Success then
	print("Outfit saved!")
else
	print("Outfit not saved")
end
explain: We wait for the player's character and its `Humanoid`.
`GetAppliedDescription()` copies the character's current look into a `HumanoidDescription`.
`PromptCreateOutfit()` shows a pop-up asking the player to save that look as an outfit.
We wait for `PromptCreateOutfitCompleted` and check if the result is `Success`.

watchOut: Calling `GetInventory()` before the player says yes to the access prompt. Always ask first and check the result.
Thinking saving an outfit gives players free items. They only get items they already own, so offer a purchase for the rest.
Expecting `PromptSaveAvatar()` to return the answer right away. Listen to `PromptSaveAvatarCompleted` instead.
